sentence: It leaves a dark ring, with a paler middle.
claim: A dried drop of a suspension leaves a ring stain: the solids collect at the drop's edge.
source_title: Deegan, Bakajin, Dupont, Huber, Nagel, Witten, 'Capillary flow as the cause of ring stains from dried liquid drops', Nature 389, 827 (1997)

sentence: They stream outward, toward the edge.

sentence: As the drop thins, the flow speeds up.
claim: In our closed-form model of a pinned drop, the outward speed of the flow grows without limit as the drop thins.
source_title: Our own simple model (compile.py, scene.mjs): a derivation, not a source
note: DERIVATION, OPEN: our model with made-up numbers; the 1997 paper predicts a power-law growth of the ring mass with time (search excerpt only). A person should check the model's behaviour against the paper.

sentence: Make the specks oval, and the ring can vanish.
claim: Ellipsoidal particles are deposited uniformly during evaporation instead of forming a ring (and surfactant restores the ring).
source_title: Yunker, Still, Lohr, Yodh, 'Suppression of the coffee-ring effect by shape-dependent capillary interactions', Nature 476, 308 (2011)
note: OPEN: search excerpt only; nature.com was unreachable from the builder session. Excerpt of the abstract: 'ellipsoidal particles are deposited uniformly during evaporation'; a news summary adds that the trick does not always work with mixtures. Hedged with 'can'.

sentence: Measure it: in this model, nine in ten specks reach the ring.
claim: In our model, with specks left in place once the drying film is thinner than a speck, about nine in ten specks (93%) end up in the ring and the rest stay in the middle.
source_title: Our own simple model (compile.py, scene.mjs): a derivation, not a source
note: DERIVATION, OPEN: our model with made-up numbers (review/model-check.md: 0.928 at the freeze point, s = 0.955). A person should re-run compile.py and check the number. Not a published result.
